name: @testlab/framework
description: The WebdriverIO runtime that generated specs are written against: resilient interactions, readable failures, and per-platform config factories.
//: Still no build step, which was always the real constraint: nothing may have to compile between generating a spec and replaying it. WebdriverIO v9 satisfies that directly — @wdio/cli depends on tsx and injects it into NODE_OPTIONS for every worker, so a .ts spec runs as-is. The two entry points differ on purpose. The runtime is TypeScript because only specs import it, and specs always run in a worker where tsx is registered. The config stays plain ESM because the *launcher* imports it, and the launcher registers tsx for itself only when the config file it was handed is TypeScript — a client project generated before this change still has a wdio.*.config.mjs, and a .ts module here would break it with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION on any Node without type stripping. Config types therefore live in config/index.d.ts, pinned against the implementation by contract.test.ts.
